note: Plain-language summaries written from the sources listed with each compound. Effect names that match the PsychonautWiki effect index (effects.json) link to its definition.

lsd.what_it_is: A semi-synthetic psychedelic made from a compound in ergot fungus, active in millionths of a gram.
lsd.how_it_works: It binds strongly to several serotonin receptors, above all the 5-HT2A receptor, and to a lesser extent to dopamine and adrenaline-type receptors. Activating 5-HT2A is what produces the psychedelic effects.
lsd.timing: Swallowed: effects begin in about 0.4 to 1 hour and last about 7 to 12 hours (Wikipedia); TripSit gives an onset of 45 to 90 minutes, 9 to 14 hours of effects and 12 to 24 hours of after-effects. Larger doses last longer.
harm_reduction: Blotter sold as LSD is sometimes an NBOMe compound instead (Erowid); a reagent test can tell them apart.
Tabs are often weaker than advertised (TripSit), so the amount on a tab is usually unknown.
TripSit advises caution with cannabis, which can intensify and change the effects.
In a dose study, 200 µg produced significant anxiety where 100 µg did not (Holze 2021).

psilocybin_mushrooms.what_it_is: A broad group of fungi from several genera that contain psilocybin; there is no single "magic mushroom" species.
psilocybin_mushrooms.how_it_works: Psilocybin is a prodrug: the body turns it into psilocin, which activates serotonin receptors. The hallucinogenic effects come from the 5-HT2A receptor, with 5-HT1A and 5-HT2C receptors possibly contributing.
psilocybin_mushrooms.timing: TripSit: common doses are often felt within two hours, sometimes up to three; effects last 4 to 6 hours, with after-effects for 1 to 24 hours.
harm_reduction: Potency varies a lot between species, strains, batches and even parts of one mushroom (Erowid: up to tenfold), so the same weight can land very differently.
Effects can take up to three hours to start (TripSit), so taking more early can stack two doses.
In a clinical dose study, 39% of volunteers had extreme anxiety or fear at the two highest doses (Griffiths 2011).

mdma.what_it_is: An entactogen ("ecstasy" as tablets, "molly" as crystals) with stimulant and mild psychedelic properties, first made in 1912.
mdma.how_it_works: It mainly makes nerve cells release more serotonin, dopamine and noradrenaline in parts of the brain.
mdma.timing: TripSit: onset 20 to 70 minutes, effects 3 to 5 hours, after-effects 1 to 72 hours.
harm_reduction: Deaths have been reported from overheating and dehydration (Wikipedia).
Short-term side effects include jaw clenching, blurred vision, sweating and a fast heart rate (Wikipedia).
In 166 volunteers, 125 mg raised blood pressure, heart rate and body temperature significantly more often than 75 mg (Vizeli and Liechti 2017).
Ecstasy tablets can contain other drugs or little MDMA (Erowid, which points to lab testing such as DrugsData).
TripSit notes that higher doses may increase neurotoxic effects.

cannabis.what_it_is: A psychoactive drug from the Cannabis plant; its main active compound is THC, one of over a hundred cannabinoids in the plant.
cannabis.how_it_works: THC partly activates the body's CB1 and CB2 cannabinoid receptors.
cannabis.timing: TripSit: smoked, onset 1 to 10 minutes and 1 to 4 hours of effects; eaten, onset 30 to 120 minutes and 4 to 10 hours of effects.
harm_reduction: Edibles take much longer to start than smoking (TripSit: 30 to 120 minutes against 1 to 10), so a second dose taken early can add on top of the first.
Cannabis use is linked to a higher risk of psychosis (Wikipedia).
Long-term regular use can lead to addiction, chronic cough and cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (repeated vomiting) (Wikipedia).
Side effects of THC include anxiety, memory impairment and drowsiness (Wikipedia).

alcohol.what_it_is: Ethanol, the active ingredient in beer, wine and spirits.
alcohol.how_it_works: A central nervous system depressant: it lowers the electrical activity of nerve cells in the brain, which causes intoxication.
alcohol.timing: TripSit: onset 15 to 30 minutes, effects 1.5 to 3 hours per drink, after-effects (hangover) 6 to 48 hours.
harm_reduction: In high amounts alcohol can cause loss of consciousness or death (Wikipedia).
Alcohol is addictive; stopping after dependence can bring withdrawal (Wikipedia).
TripSit suggests spreading drinks over a few hours with water in between, and checking labels for alcohol content.
TripSit lists alcohol among the combinations to avoid for GHB, benzodiazepines and ketamine.

caffeine.what_it_is: A stimulant of the methylxanthine class found in coffee, tea, soft drinks and tablets; the most widely used psychoactive drug.
caffeine.how_it_works: It blocks adenosine receptors, so adenosine's calming, sleep-promoting signal is held back.
caffeine.timing: TripSit: onset 5 to 10 minutes, effects 1.5 to 5 hours.
harm_reduction: Pills and powders make it possible to take a dangerous amount by accident; a whole box of caffeine tablets at once can be fatal (Erowid).
Daily use can cause mild dependence, with headache, sleepiness and irritability when stopping (Wikipedia).
Some health authorities advise pregnant women to limit caffeine (Wikipedia).

nicotine.what_it_is: A stimulant alkaloid found mainly in tobacco, also made synthetically for vapes, pouches, gum and patches.
nicotine.how_it_works: It activates nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, which releases dopamine, acetylcholine and noradrenaline.
nicotine.timing: Erowid: smoked, onset within a minute and effects 10 to 30 minutes; gum and other oral forms, onset 2 to 15 minutes and effects 1 to 2 hours.
harm_reduction: Nicotine is highly addictive; withdrawal brings irritability, anxiety and trouble concentrating (Wikipedia).
Products list the nicotine they contain, not what is absorbed, and smokers adjust how much they take in without noticing (Erowid).
Slower forms such as patches and gum deliver lower doses and are used to help people stop smoking (Wikipedia).

ketamine.what_it_is: A dissociative anaesthetic used in medicine for anaesthesia, pain and treatment-resistant depression.
ketamine.how_it_works: It blocks the NMDA receptor, a receptor for the brain's main excitatory messenger, glutamate.
ketamine.timing: TripSit: snorted, onset 7.5 to 20 minutes; swallowed, 10 to 75 minutes; effects 1 to 2 hours and after-effects 1 to 2 hours.
harm_reduction: TripSit advises against driving, walking around or other motor activity while under its effects.
Mixing with other depressants such as alcohol, benzodiazepines or opioids is listed as risky by TripSit.

cocaine.what_it_is: A stimulant from the leaves of the coca plant.
cocaine.how_it_works: It blocks the reuptake of serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine, so they stay active between nerve cells for longer.
cocaine.timing: TripSit: rapid onset, effects 1 to 1.5 hours, after-effects 1 to 4 hours.
harm_reduction: It can narrow blood vessels and raise heart rate, blood pressure and body temperature; overdose can cause stroke, heart attack or sudden cardiac death (Wikipedia).
Chronic use can lead to dependence and damage inside the nose (Wikipedia).
Purity varies widely (TripSit), so the same amount can be much stronger than expected.

amphetamine.what_it_is: A stimulant prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy, and also used recreationally.
amphetamine.how_it_works: It increases the activity of noradrenaline and dopamine (and other monoamines) in the brain.
amphetamine.timing: TripSit: swallowed, onset 15 to 30 minutes and effects 4 to 8 hours; snorted, onset 5 to 10 minutes and effects 3 to 6 hours.
harm_reduction: Recreational doses are usually far larger than prescribed ones and carry a much greater risk of serious side effects; heavy use risks addiction (Wikipedia).
TripSit advises against mixing with other stimulants or with depressants, which strains the heart.
Street amphetamine is often impure (TripSit), so a purer batch can be much stronger.

methamphetamine.what_it_is: A potent stimulant, used mostly recreationally and rarely as a second-line ADHD treatment.
methamphetamine.how_it_works: It makes nerve cells release serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine.
methamphetamine.timing: TripSit: swallowed, onset 20 to 70 minutes and effects 10 to 12 hours; smoked or injected, onset within 2 minutes; after-effects around 24 hours, longer with redosing.
harm_reduction: Overdose or long binges can cause psychosis, muscle breakdown, seizures and bleeding in the brain (Wikipedia).
It carries a high risk of compulsive use and dependence, and high doses damage dopamine nerve cells (Wikipedia).
TripSit lists using it within 14 days of an MAOI as something to avoid.

dmt.what_it_is: A short-acting psychedelic tryptamine found in many plants and animals; brewed with an MAOI it is the basis of ayahuasca.
dmt.how_it_works: It binds to many receptors, most strongly serotonin receptors (5-HT2A, 5-HT1A, 5-HT2C), which are thought to cause its effects. Swallowed alone it is broken down before it can act; an MAOI prevents that.
dmt.timing: TripSit: smoked or vaporised, onset within 2 minutes and effects 3 to 10 minutes; taken by mouth with an MAOI, onset 20 to 45 minutes and effects 3 to 7 hours.
harm_reduction: It may cause acute psychological distress or heart and blood-pressure effects, especially in people predisposed to them (Wikipedia).
The chance of an overwhelming "breakthrough" rises with dose, and vaporising is not fully efficient, so the dose received varies (TripSit).
Taken by mouth it needs an MAOI (Wikipedia), and an MAOI changes how other drugs act: TripSit, for example, lists methamphetamine within 14 days of an MAOI as something to avoid.

mescaline.what_it_is: A naturally occurring psychedelic from cacti such as peyote and San Pedro, used recreationally, spiritually and in research.
mescaline.how_it_works: It mainly partly activates the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor; blocking that receptor with ketanserin blocks its effects.
mescaline.timing: TripSit: onset 60 to 180 minutes or more, effects 6 to 12 hours. In a clinical study, effects lasted from about 6 hours (100 mg) to 14 hours (800 mg) (Klaiber 2024).
harm_reduction: Slow onset (TripSit) makes it easy to take more before the first dose has arrived.
Nausea and vomiting were frequent at the highest dose studied (Klaiber 2024).
Doses differ between mescaline salts and cactus material; published charts are for mescaline hydrochloride (TripSit, Erowid).

2c-b.what_it_is: A psychedelic of the phenethylamine (2C) family, usually taken by mouth.
2c-b.how_it_works: It partly activates serotonin 5-HT2 receptors, including 5-HT2A.
2c-b.timing: TripSit: swallowed, onset 20 to 75 minutes and effects 4 to 8 hours; snorted, onset 1 to 10 minutes and effects 2 to 4 hours.
harm_reduction: Snorted it acts within minutes, swallowed it can take over an hour (TripSit), so effects and timing differ a lot by route.

ghb.what_it_is: A depressant that also occurs naturally in the brain as a signalling molecule.
ghb.how_it_works: It acts on its own GHB receptor and weakly activates the GABA-B receptor, slowing the nervous system.
ghb.timing: TripSit: onset 20 to 60 minutes, effects 1.5 to 2.5 hours, after-effects 2 to 4 hours.
harm_reduction: The step from heavy sleep to overdose is short: Erowid lists heavy sleep at 3 to 5 g, overdose at 5 to 10 g and risk of death above that.
TripSit lists alcohol, benzodiazepines and other depressants as combinations to avoid.

alprazolam.what_it_is: A fast-acting benzodiazepine (Xanax) prescribed for anxiety and panic disorder.
alprazolam.how_it_works: Like other benzodiazepines, it boosts the effect of GABA, the brain's main calming messenger, at GABA-A receptors.
alprazolam.timing: TripSit: onset 15 to 40 minutes, effects 5 to 8 hours, after-effects 6 to 24 hours.
harm_reduction: Higher doses raise the chance of blacking out (TripSit).
After long use, stopping suddenly is strongly advised against (TripSit); the prescribing label describes a gradual taper.
Combining with alcohol or other depressants is listed to avoid (TripSit).

diazepam.what_it_is: A long-acting benzodiazepine (Valium) used for anxiety, seizures, alcohol withdrawal and muscle spasms.
diazepam.how_it_works: It increases the effect of GABA, the brain's main calming messenger.
diazepam.timing: TripSit: onset 30 to 90 minutes, effects 10 to 24 hours, after-effects up to several days.
harm_reduction: Long use leads to tolerance and dependence, with withdrawal when the dose is reduced (Wikipedia).
Rare serious side effects include slowed breathing (Wikipedia); other depressants add to it (TripSit).
Its long action means effects can carry into the next day (TripSit).

clonazepam.what_it_is: A benzodiazepine (Klonopin) used for anxiety disorders and seizures.
clonazepam.how_it_works: It binds to GABA-A receptors and increases the effect of GABA, the brain's main calming messenger.
clonazepam.timing: TripSit: onset 20 to 45 minutes, effects 8 to 12 hours, after-effects 8 to 48 hours.
harm_reduction: Dependence develops in about one in three people who take benzodiazepines for more than four weeks (Wikipedia).
TripSit lists all other central nervous system depressants as combinations to avoid.

oxycodone.what_it_is: A semi-synthetic opioid painkiller (OxyContin, Roxicodone and others).
oxycodone.timing: TripSit: immediate-release by mouth, onset about 20 minutes and effects 4 to 6 hours; extended-release, effects 6 to 8 hours.
harm_reduction: It is highly addictive, and stopping quickly after regular use brings withdrawal (Wikipedia).
Slowed breathing is the main danger, and other depressants add to it (Wikipedia, TripSit).

morphine.what_it_is: An opiate found naturally in opium poppies, used mainly as a painkiller.
morphine.how_it_works: It acts directly on the central nervous system to relieve pain and change how pain is felt.
morphine.timing: TripSit: immediate-release by mouth, onset 10 to 30 minutes and effects 4 to 6 hours.
harm_reduction: Serious side effects include slowed breathing, vomiting and low blood pressure (Wikipedia).
It is highly addictive, and reducing the dose after long use brings withdrawal (Wikipedia).

codeine.what_it_is: An opiate used for pain, cough and diarrhoea, often combined with paracetamol (acetaminophen).
codeine.how_it_works: The liver turns codeine into morphine; how fast depends on a person's genes, so the same dose can act very differently between people.
codeine.timing: TripSit: onset 30 to 45 minutes, effects 3 to 6 hours.
harm_reduction: Many codeine products also contain paracetamol (acetaminophen); TripSit warns against taking too much of it alongside other products that contain it.
It can cause breathing difficulties and addiction (Wikipedia).

tramadol.what_it_is: An opioid painkiller that also works on serotonin and noradrenaline.
tramadol.how_it_works: The liver turns it into O-desmethyltramadol, a stronger opioid; tramadol itself also blocks the reuptake of serotonin and noradrenaline.
tramadol.timing: TripSit: first effects after about an hour, peak blood levels at about 4 hours, effects 5 to 7 hours.
harm_reduction: It can cause seizures and serotonin syndrome (Wikipedia); TripSit notes it lowers the seizure threshold and that recreational effects have a ceiling.
TripSit lists benzodiazepines, alcohol and other opioids as combinations to avoid.

kratom.what_it_is: The leaves of Mitragyna speciosa, a tropical tree from Southeast Asia.
kratom.how_it_works: Its alkaloids (mainly mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine) partly activate the μ-opioid receptor. Some people find it stimulating, probably not through the usual stimulant mechanisms.
kratom.timing: TripSit: onset 10 to 40 minutes, effects 2 to 5 hours.
harm_reduction: Serious side effects can include slowed breathing, seizures, psychosis and liver injury; regular use can lead to addiction and withdrawal (Wikipedia).
Most deaths linked to kratom involved other substances as well (Wikipedia).
Strength varies between batches and products, and extract-enhanced products are far stronger than plain leaf (TripSit, Erowid).

dextromethorphan.what_it_is: A cough suppressant found in many cough and cold medicines, which acts as a dissociative at high doses.
dextromethorphan.how_it_works: At high doses it and its metabolite dextrorphan block the NMDA receptor, like ketamine; it also blocks serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake and activates sigma-1 receptors.
dextromethorphan.timing: TripSit: onset 20 to 60 minutes, effects 6 to 8 hours, after-effects up to 12 hours.
harm_reduction: Many cough products contain other active ingredients that are dangerous in large amounts, such as chlorpheniramine (CPM) or paracetamol; check the label (Erowid).
TripSit gives doses per kilogram of body weight and reports deaths at very high amounts.

nitrous.what_it_is: Nitrous oxide ("laughing gas"), a gas used in medicine and food that is inhaled for a brief high.
nitrous.how_it_works: It is not broken down by the body; inhaled, it causes euphoria, dissociation and relaxation within seconds.
nitrous.timing: TripSit: onset within a minute, effects 1 to 5 minutes, after-effects 15 to 30 minutes.
harm_reduction: Rare deaths and injuries come from lack of oxygen or from accidents, often alongside alcohol (Wikipedia).
Heavy, frequent use can cause vitamin B12 deficiency and lasting nerve damage, including to the spinal cord (Wikipedia).

methylphenidate.what_it_is: A stimulant (Ritalin, Concerta) prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy.
methylphenidate.how_it_works: It is believed to work by blocking the reuptake of dopamine and noradrenaline.
methylphenidate.timing: TripSit: immediate-release, onset 30 to 120 minutes and effects 3 to 6 hours; extended-release, effects 8 to 12 hours; crushing an extended-release tablet makes it act like immediate-release.
harm_reduction: Common side effects include loss of appetite, poor sleep and small rises in heart rate and blood pressure (Wikipedia).
Dependence and withdrawal are mainly reported with high-dose or non-medical use (Wikipedia).
